Bruno Mars.text: As a child in Honolulu he was known around Hawaii for his Elvis Presley impersonation.
Bruno Mars.evidence: Raised in Honolulu, Mars gained recognition in Hawaii as a child for his impersonation of Elvis Presley, before moving to Los Angeles in 2003 to pursue a musical career.

Rihanna.text: After her audition, Jay-Z was told not to let her leave the building without a deal; she waited in his office.
Rihanna.evidence: Jay-Z was convinced of her potential, and Reid told him not to let her leave the building without a deal. She waited in Jay-Z's office while lawyers finalized a six-album contract with Def Jam.

The Weeknd.text: He took the name after moving to Parkdale on a weekend, dropping an e to avoid a band called the Weekend.
The Weeknd.evidence: He adopted his stage name because he moved to Parkdale on a weekend; he removed the last 'e' in 'weekend' to avoid trademark issues with the Canadian pop rock band the Weekend.

Justin Bieber.text: Justin Timberlake reportedly lost the race to sign him, partly over fears that two Justins would confuse the market.
Justin Bieber.evidence: Singer Justin Timberlake was reportedly also in the running to sign Bieber but lost the bidding war to Usher, partly due to concerns that two associated singers of the same name would confuse the market.

Taylor Swift.text: Named after James Taylor, she got a unisex name because her parents hoped it would help her succeed in business.
Taylor Swift.evidence: She is named after the singer-songwriter James Taylor; her parents chose a unisex name, hoping it would help her succeed in business.

Lady Gaga.text: Producer Rob Fusari says the name was born when his phone autocorrected a text calling her "Radio Ga Ga".
Lady Gaga.evidence: He said they began dating in May 2006, and claimed he was the first person to call her "Lady Gaga", which was derived from the Queen song "Radio Ga Ga". According to Fusari, the name was coined when he attempted to call her "Radio Ga Ga" in a text message, and his phone's spell checker autocorrected "Radio" to "Lady".

Drake.text: His first mixtape earned him $304.04 in royalties, and his first concert, opening for Ice Cube, paid $100.
Drake.evidence: Room for Improvement was released for sale only and sold roughly 6,000 copies, for which Drake received $304.04 in royalties. He performed his first concert on August 19, 2006, at the Kool Haus nightclub as an opening act for Ice Cube, performing for half an hour and earning $100.

Ariana Grande.text: At eight she sang the national anthem at a Florida Panthers game and performed in a cruise ship karaoke lounge.
Ariana Grande.evidence: At age eight, she sang "The Star-Spangled Banner" at the Florida Panthers' home game against the Chicago Blackhawks on January 16, 2002. ... At age eight, she performed at a karaoke lounge on a cruise ship and with orchestras such as South Florida's Philharmonic, Florida Sunshine Pops, and Symphonic Orchestras.

Coldplay.text: Will Champion became their drummer because the band came to recruit his roommate, who never showed up.
Coldplay.evidence: He said that Martin, Buckland and Berryman came to his house because his roommate was a good drummer with a drum kit; however, when the roommate did not arrive, Champion played instead.

Bad Bunny.text: His stage name comes from a time he was forced to wear a bunny costume and was annoyed about it.
Bad Bunny.evidence: His stage name originated from a time when he was forced to wear a bunny costume and was annoyed about it.
